newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya's Gaddafi says Clinton a nice guy.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi says Clinton a nice guy.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi still had some warm words for U.S. President Bill Clinton while accusing the United States for manufacturing the AIDs virus.
"Clinton is believed to be a nice man. He is not from the World War II generation. His file is blank," Gaddafi said at a meeting with Tunisian students in Tunis.
"But he (Clinton) is a poor (guy), even if he loves peace, he doesn't rule. The ruler is the imperialism, the big firms, the Jewish lobby," he said on Wednesday.
Gaddafi, accused by the United States of sponsoring terrorism, had described Clinton as a friend earlier this year on the 10-year anniversary of U.S. air strikes on Libya.
The Libyan leader also told the meeting the United States was behind the spread of the AIDS virus.

"This American state is responsible for AIDS," he said. "The U.S. intelligence had been manufacturing microbiologic arms and found the AIDS virus. They experimented with it on prisoners from Haiti some of which were later released. The virus spread from there and the prisoners later died."
Gaddafi said Libya had officially asked the World Health Organisation (WHO) to force the United States to hand over an alleged smallpox virus.
"They (the United States) refused but Libya still insist for the United States to hand it over to the WHO," he said.
The United Nations imposed sanctions on Libya in 1992 for its refusal to turn over two suspects wanted for the bombing of a Pan Am jet over Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988.
